summary.text: 钱 is the standardized simplified form of 錢. The traditional graph combines 金, which marks a metal-related category, with 戔, a probable sound component. Both an agricultural-tool use and a money use are recorded; their historical connection is uncertain.

formation.text: The traditional graph 錢 is phonosemantic: 金 contributes a metal-related category, and 戔 is analyzed as the sound component. 钱 writes these with the corresponding simplified forms 钅 and 戋. This construction is an old dictionary analysis, not direct proof of the graph’s earliest formation.

components.text: In 錢, 金 is the left-side semantic component, marking a metal-related category. In 钱, the corresponding left-side form is 钅.

In 錢, 戔 is analyzed as the right-side phonetic component. It is written 戋 in simplified 钱; modern and reconstructed comparisons fit the proposed sound role, though they do not establish its full historical sound relation.

sound_limitation.text: The comparisons are compatible with a phonetic role but do not establish a complete regular sound history or independently prove the component’s ancient role.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 戔 jiān and 錢 qián are similar but not identical; these readings alone do not establish their historical relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart 2014 Middle Chinese, 戔 dzan and 錢 dzjen are similar, a comparison compatible with a phonetic role.
In Baxter–Sagart 2014 Old Chinese, 戔 *[dz]ˤa[n] and 錢 *N-ts[a][n] are compatible with a phonetic role; this comparison does not establish a complete regular sound history.

components.text: 戋 is the simplified right-side form corresponding to 戔 in 錢. The phonetic analysis belongs to 戔 within 錢; this record identifies only the graphic correspondence in 钱.

history.text: 錢 corresponds to simplified 钱. Its traditional components 金 and 戔 appear in 钱 as 钅 and 戋; this graphic simplification does not itself imply a change in meaning.
Seal-script and manuscript form categories are recorded, but they do not provide a dated, inspectable sequence explaining how the graph’s shape developed.

uncertainties.text: The earliest secure attestation and a form-by-form graphic history for 錢 remain unresolved.

Modern and reconstructed comparisons fit the analysis of 戔 as a phonetic component, but its full ancient sound history remains unsettled. Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang values belong to separate reconstruction systems.

senses.period: dating unresolved; cited in transmitted Odes wording and defined in the Han-era Shuowen account
senses.text: The Shuowen account defines 錢 as an ancient field implement, and a cited Odes line names it among agricultural tools. The wording’s exact date is unresolved.

senses.period: attested in cited Guoyu and Shiji passages; first use not dated
senses.text: 錢 occurs in cited monetary contexts, including passages about casting large coins and marked copper coins. These attest the money sense in the cited texts but do not date its first use.
钱 means money, currency, or coins.
A recorded use has the meaning “fees”; its date and connection to other senses are unresolved.
A recorded use refers to coin-shaped objects; its chronology and connection to other senses are unresolved.
A recorded use is a unit of weight; its date and connection to other senses are unresolved.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but their semantic connection is not demonstrated. A link through tool-shaped currency has been proposed but remains conjectural for this word.

limitations.text: The Odes citation supports a field-implement use in the transmitted text, but the wording’s date is unresolved. The cited monetary examples do not date the beginning of that sense.
How the field-tool and money senses are historically connected remains unresolved; the graph’s phonetic analysis does not explain their semantic relationship.

overview.text: 钱 is the simplified form of 錢. The traditional graph combines 金 for a metal-related category with 戔 as a proposed sound component. Both field-tool and money uses are recorded, but their connection is uncertain.

components.text: In 錢, 金 marks a metal-related category; 钱 uses its corresponding left-side form 钅.
In 錢, 戔 is analyzed as the sound component; 钱 writes it in the simplified form 戋.
戋 is the simplified written form corresponding to 戔 in 錢.

relationships.text: 钱 is identified as the standardized simplified form of 錢; the traditional component forms 金 and 戔 correspond to 钅 and 戋 in 钱.
金 contributes a metal-related semantic category in traditional 錢 and corresponds to the left-side form 钅 in simplified 钱.
戔 is analyzed as the phonetic component in 錢. Modern Mandarin and Baxter–Sagart comparisons fit this role but do not prove the full historical sound relation; 戔 corresponds to 戋 in simplified 钱.
